extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulewriters, agency staff, regulators, and stakeholders submitting or evaluating CAA §112 (MACT) rulemakings for the oil & gas sector
extracted.subtask_description: Public-interest comment letter giving detailed legal, technical, and procedural criteria EPA must follow in setting MACT floors, beyond-the-floor levels, monitoring, compliance, and enforcement for oil & gas source categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: MACT floor determination must consider multiple factors (not just control technology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control technology is only one factor in determining emissions levels of the best performing similar sources; EPA cannot base floors exclusively on technology and must consider other factors such as fuel inputs and raw materials (Nat’l Lime Ass’n v. U.S. EPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identifying the best performing similar source, EPA must include non-technology factors (e.g., fuel inputs, raw materials) in addition to control technology. Courts require that the floor reflect what the best controlled similar source achieves across relevant factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: MACT floor must be determined without regard to costs or other excluded factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The MACT “floor” must be determined “without regard to costs or other factors and methods listed in section 7412(d)(2).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must set floors based on performance alone as required by statute and controlling case law (e.g., Nat’l Lime Ass’n; NRDC v. EPA). Cost considerations cannot be used to lower the floor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use current, representative emissions data (do not rely on outdated legacy data)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA cannot rely on old/1997 legacy data to set numeric standards when more recent, higher-quality emissions data are available; the agency must provide reasoned explanation of how legacy data represent currently operating units or else using them is arbitrary and capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If higher-quality recent data exist (e.g., 2005 NEI or state data), EPA must use or reconcile them; justify representativeness of any legacy dataset and document industry/technology changes that could affect emissions estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess top-performing units based on up-to-date technology performance
rubrics_metrics.description: An assessment today of the controls and emission rates from the top performing dehydration units would result in more accurate estimates for potential emissions reductions; EPA's claim that processes haven’t changed must be substantiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should collect or analyze current emissions/control-performance data from a varied group of sources and explain why those data represent best performers; do not assume 1997 performance reflects current best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set MACT floors and numeric limits for all listed HAPs emitted (not just selected surrogates like BTEX)
rubrics_metrics.description: When setting MACT for the first time for a source (e.g., small glycol dehydrators), EPA must set numerical limits on BTEX pollutants and on other HAPs emitted by these sources per 42 U.S.C. § 7412(d)(1),(2),(3),(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA cannot limit regulation to only BTEX without explaining a lawful surrogate approach; if other HAPs (e.g., n-hexane, 2,2,4-trimethylpentane, ethylene glycol) are emitted, EPA must set numeric limits or validly justify any surrogate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: If using a surrogate pollutant, demonstrate and memorialize correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must demonstrate that a correlation exists between two pollutants when deciding to use a surrogate, and memorialize that correlation in a fashion that commenters, the public, regulated entities, or a reviewing court can assess (Mossville Envtl. Action Now; Nat’l Lime Ass’n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide statistical/technical evidence of correlation and record rationale in rulemaking materials so surrogate use is transparent and reviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on emission factors alone to identify category emissions or best performers
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission factors are based on the average results of limited testing of some sources within the sector and cannot be relied on to determine the emissions profile of the category or to identify the best performing sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If EPA uses emission factors, it must supplement them with monitoring, representative testing, or other data proving they reflect true performance across the category; explain limitations of factors in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require robust monitoring and verification when emission factors are used
rubrics_metrics.description: If using emission factors, EPA must require robust monitoring to ensure transparency and effective enforcement, including continuous measurement from a sufficient number of monitors and regular verification and oversight by the permitting agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring requirements must enable accurate, clear reporting of emissions reductions for all HAPs; electronic reporting and public disclosure are required so citizens may enforce the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt numeric, pollutant-specific standards and unit-specific limits where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should adopt numeric standards for the individual pollutants and adopt monitoring and enforcement measures that require facilities to accurately and clearly report emissions reductions; proposed unit-specific BTEX limits for small dehydrators are an example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set numeric limits by pollutant (and by unit where necessary) rather than broad percent reductions or single-device surrogates; specify units (e.g., grams BTEX/scm-ppmv) and apply to existing and new sources as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: MACT floor for previously uncontrolled storage vessels must be properly calculated (not copied from 1997)
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing MACT limits for previously uncontrolled storage vessels, EPA cannot simply set the MACT floor at the level reached in the 1997 rulemaking; it must provide adequate justification and demonstrate representativeness of the underlying data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a fresh analysis per statutory requirements, explain why any older data are representative, and consider technological developments and industry changes since prior rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a thorough and well-supported technology review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA’s technology review for storage vessel control technologies must be comprehensive and avoid incorrect assumptions; without support the public cannot understand or EPA justify its decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the technology assessment (methods, data sources, representativeness) and address uncertainties or limits explicitly; correct prior flawed assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform updated beyond-the-floor analyses for newly controlled emission points
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must determine the “maximum degree of reduction in emissions” achievable for newly controlled emission points (e.g., small glycol dehydrators and storage vessels) as required by 42 U.S.C. § 7412(d)(2); the proposed rule must include beyond-the-floor discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After properly determining the MACT floor, EPA must conduct beyond-the-floor analyses using current emission control data and document the analyses and conclusions in rulemaking materials (Nat’l Lime Ass’n precedent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set MACT limits for all currently uncontrolled HAP emission points found in the sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is legally required to set a MACT limit for emissions from all of the emission points identified in the oil & gas sectors (including those previously unregulated); its 112(d)(6) review reopens and requires full review and revision where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify every significant HAP emission point, evaluate data, and adopt standards where necessary; do not leave unlawful gaps from the original MACT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasoned explanation for any emission points or HAPs the agency chooses not to control
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must provide a reasoned analysis of sources it chooses not to control under the proposed rules because it believes other NESHAPs will adequately control those emissions — describing characteristics and how they’re controlled and whether those other NESHAPs have been updated under §112(d)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain technical basis and currentness of other NESHAPs relied upon; document that such measures cover the emissions and have been revised as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze comprehensive set of emission points and select appropriate scope of covered HAP sources
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must evaluate a comprehensive set of emissions points at major sources and, based on technical arguments and current data, select the range of HAP sources within the sectors to be covered by the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use current data reflecting industry expansion/changes; ensure major contributors are included so public health is protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure regulation of every HAP emitted (do not rely on incomplete NEI data claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA cannot assert that a limited set of HAPs comprise virtually all emissions when emission estimates for key HAPs were missing for many facilities; EPA must ensure that it is regulating and setting a limit for every HAP emitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address data gaps (e.g., NEI missing estimates for 75% of facilities) and justify any summary claims with transparent data analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close gaps for uncontrolled VHAPs and avoid single-device-based percent reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must set standards for uncontrolled VHAPs rather than continuing to set only a total percent reduction based on the performance of a single device; reliance on unsubstantiated assumptions is unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representative system-level performance data rather than single-device estimates; document assumptions and uncertainties explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude significant emission points from 'associated equipment' only after analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposes to exclude storage vessels and glycol dehydrators from 'associated equipment'; agency must analyze whether other similarly situated components should also be excluded and explain decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each emission point considered for exclusion, provide analysis of significance, data supporting exclusion, and public documentation so the public can understand scope and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: No start-up/shutdown/malfunction (SSM) exemptions or 'excused excursion' provisions allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 112 requires standards to apply at all times; EPA may not lawfully include any 'excused excursion' (e.g., one excused excursion per semiannual period) or other SSM exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove all SSM exceptions from the rules and ensure standards are continuous in operation per Sierra Club v. EPA and statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not promulgate an affirmative defense to civil penalties for malfunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA’s proposed affirmative defense to penalties for malfunctions exceeds agency authority, conflicts with the CAA statutory scheme for civil penalties and citizen suits, and would unduly chill citizen enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency regulations cannot bar courts from applying the statutory list of factors for civil penalties (42 U.S.C. § 7413(e)) or otherwise limit civil penalties available under citizen suits; EPA should withdraw any affirmative defense proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalties must be assessed by courts using statutory factors; agency cannot preempt
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress intended courts to apply prescribed factors in assessing civil penalties (42 U.S.C. § 7413(e)); EPA lacks authority to create rules that prevent courts from considering or imposing penalties under CAA §304.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not promulgate regulations that attempt to modify or limit judicial penalty determinations; ensure rule language and preamble respect the statutory enforcement framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid imposing burdens that chill citizen enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: An affirmative defense or technical barriers that force citizens into fact-intensive disputes over malfunctions will hinder citizen participation and undermine the Act's enforcement goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design must preserve citizens’ ability to enforce the Act effectively without added burdens that impede relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: If an affirmative defense were allowed (contrary to commenters’ view), require compensatory penalties dedicated to local enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming arguendo EPA had authority, commenters propose that a specific amount of compensatory penalties should apply to each reported malfunction and funds be dedicated to enforcement, inspections, and monitoring in the local community around the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design compensatory penalties to fund community-focused enforcement and oversight to reduce recurrence of malfunctions (commenters nonetheless urge EPA not to adopt an affirmative defense).

rubrics_metrics.name: If an affirmative defense were allowed, limit its use by facility (e.g., once per 10 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must modify regulations so that the affirmative defense cannot be used by a specific facility or company more than once within a set period of time (suggestion: 10 years); availability should be automatic ly revoked if prior malfunction within that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is proposed only as a mitigation measure; commenters assert the affirmative defense should not be adopted at all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate public reporting and rapid community notification for malfunctions/exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must promulgate public reporting and notification requirements such that when a facility notifies EPA of a malfunction or exceedance, the notice is made publicly available on EPA's website within 14 days and community notification is made within 2 business days through local channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications should include all known emissions information so the public can evaluate health risks; use facility website, municipality/school notices, press releases, radio/TV to reach neighbors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not permit manufacturer-only testing for combustion control devices
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should not allow a manufacturer-only test for combustion devices because such testing cannot anticipate local conditions that may adversely affect performance and does not allow EPA/state/citizens to verify ongoing compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require independent verification or field testing that accounts for local operational conditions and enables regulator and public oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require electronic reporting and immediate public disclosure of monitoring/test reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters support EPA’s proposal for electronic reporting as vital to strengthen enforcement and transparency; EPA must require immediate disclosure on the Internet without need for FOIA for all collected reports (initial and periodic test results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make reports publicly available promptly to support citizen enforcement and community awareness; ensure data formats and accessibility facilitate public use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply periodic testing requirements to all control devices including condensers
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA’s periodic testing requirements proposed for non-condenser control devices should apply to all devices, including condensers; EPA fails to justify excluding condensers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate the design evaluation alternative and require periodic testing across device types; report results electronically and promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require continuous monitoring of glycol dehydrators (with case-by-case exceptions only)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must require continuous monitoring of glycol dehydrators rather than broadly exempting them due to practical concerns; practical exceptions should be handled case-by-case rather than weakening the national rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish continuous monitoring requirements, and if specific facilities demonstrate impracticability, provide narrowly tailored, documented exemptions instead of a categorical exclusion.
